questions.text: A hospital tracks the number of patient falls on a medical-surgical unit each month. What type of data does this represent?
questions.explanation: Discrete. Falls are countable whole numbers with no fractional values. This is the defining characteristic of discrete data. Nominal data has no order, ordinal has ranked categories, and continuous data is measured on a scale.

questions.text: A quality analyst is reviewing temperature readings in Celsius from a post-operative unit and comparing them to blood pressure readings. Which statement about these data types is MOST accurate for statistical analysis?

options.a: Both are ratio data with a true zero and support full mathematical comparison
options.b: Temperature is interval data; blood pressure is ratio data
options.c: Both are interval data with no true zero
options.d: Temperature is ratio data; blood pressure is ordinal data

questions.explanation: Temperature in Celsius has an arbitrary zero point making it interval data. Blood pressure has a true zero meaning absence of pressure making it ratio data. Ratio data supports valid comparison and benchmarking while interval data does not support ratio statements.

questions.text: A Decision Support System identifies that a hospital's CLABSI rate is 2.8 per 1,000 line days compared to a national benchmark of 1.1. Which DSS function is being performed?
questions.explanation: Benchmark Performance. This function compares results against competitors and industry benchmarks. Outcomes Management involves analyzing outcomes to support improvement plans which would be the next logical step after benchmarking.

questions.text: A quality team conducts patient interviews in the emergency department to understand why patients feel their pain is inadequately managed. What type of data collection method is this and what is its primary purpose?

options.a: Quantitative; to measure frequency and magnitude of the problem
options.b: Qualitative; to explore why and how the problem is experienced
options.c: Prospective; to predict future pain management gaps
options.d: Administrative; to document compliance with pain protocols

questions.explanation: Interviews are a qualitative data collection tool. They explore why something happens and how people experience it, providing rich contextual understanding rather than numerical frequency data.

questions.text: When clinical data is analyzed WITHOUT integration with administrative data such as staffing or scheduling, what key analytical risk does this create?

options.b: Inability to calculate ratios from discrete data

questions.explanation: Analyzing clinical outcomes without administrative context hides systemic root causes. Staffing shortages, scheduling gaps, or resource constraints that drive clinical outcomes remain invisible when data systems are siloed.
